Executive summary (say it): In Q3, BCC ran its first integrated marketing campaign, expanded programming across Atlanta, New York and Los Angeles, and launched a Beyond the Game social channel that drew over 15,000 viewers in three weeks. Fundraising stands at $1.532M, 51% of the $3M goal, including $920K from Apple. $8.9M pending, most decisions in October. The LXP now supports all BCC and BGC programming. We enter Q4 with 485+ learners served, a six-month impact report in progress, and a year-end giving campaign on the calendar.

[ P2 · Online Learning Platform ]
The LXP

Home for the Summer ran on it, start to finish, in one week.

One platform now runs both organizations

275Learners
7Courses, BCC + BGC
$67KYearly tools it replaces
  • In Q2 it was a closed beta with four programs. Now it supports both BCC and Black Girls Code, with new courses launching nearly every week.
  • BGC's Roblox and Endless Games Virtual Bootcamps ran entirely on the platform this quarter. That used to take several separate tools, an estimated $67,000 a year.
  • Built-in pre, mid and post surveys mean every cohort measures its own growth. Home for the Summer ran entirely on the LXP in a single week. When it ended, we showed NextEra Energy exactly what their learners gained, pulled straight from the platform.

KPI: all BCC and BGC programming on the LXP by EOY '26 · Complete

[ P3 · Operationalize Centers ]
Atlanta

Rep. Kim Schofield at the Atlanta Center

Where the Centers go next

AtlantaThe ATDC residency formally ended Aug 31, and ATDC asked us to keep hosting there through year end. Q4 moves to a monthly cadence at two satellites: ATDC for entrepreneurs and local leaders, and SolePlay, a community space owned by a prospective Atlanta advisory board member. State Rep. Kim Schofield brokered introductions to six state representatives and city council members, leading to our first government pilot: City of South Fulton, $30K, decision in October.
New YorkActive discussion with a prospective site partner. Decision before year end.
Los AngelesTwo Center Experiences in October: a fundraising and ecosystem dinner with a hands-on build, and a four-week Saturday morning program for middle schoolers at a partner site. Community re-engagement first, so we pick the right location before a larger footprint.
NextStrong signals from Connecticut, Rancho Cordova, Washington DC, Baltimore and West Palm Beach. ServiceNow's Chief Workforce Innovation Officer Karen Pavlin is discussing a Center floor and a Beyond the Game keynote at their 2027 conference.

KPI: ATL, then NYC, then LA by Q4 · On track · West Palm Beach and ServiceNow pending funding and timing for 2027

Rep. Schofield is a sitting official: confirm she is comfortable with her photo and name on a board slide if shared beyond the meeting.

[ Home for the Summer · with NextEra Energy ]
In their
own words
Ty
Isaac

A week-long intensive for undergraduates

College students fall into a gap most people don't talk about: ambition but no access, rarely encouraged to build a portfolio outside class, and little exposure to how real digital work moves. Home for the Summer supports them in the last stretch of summer.

"As a young adult who has autism, I am so grateful; this program has given me confidence in ways I did not think were even possible."

[ Ty ]

"I'm leaving with new connections, a clearer vision for what's next, and even more motivation to keep moving forward."

[ Isaac ]

Each video is that participant's own testimonial, so face and quote match. Click to play with sound.

Built into a university syllabus

We designed a series of shorter-format sessions, 90 to 120 minutes, and are gearing up for a strong close to the year.

A professor at the University of Michigan has built Catalyst Labs workshops into her course syllabus, bringing 25 graduate students per workshop into direct engagement with Beyond Code programming, on top of our own recruitment.

[ Additional Program Updates ]
IT to
Cyber
Learners in the cohort13

Two more programs in motion

IT to Cybersecurity

The cohort stands at 13 learners. Recent coaching sessions led to format adjustments to better position the cohort for certification success. Cohort quality over raw enrollment is how we build programming that holds.

Field Ready · piloted this quarter

Our answer to growing demand for forward-deployed technical talent: for anyone who needs to operate confidently with technology in the field, not in a classroom or a traditional office.

Entrepreneur Shonda Scott took part in the pilot and gave a testimonial. Her podcast with Oprah Winfrey released this week; her book centers on trying twelve new things, and Field Ready was one of them. Early engagement has been strong.

Doc detail kept here: two IT to Cyber participants were removed due to commitment concerns. Confirm Shonda Scott's permission to be named.
